meta.howToRead: Each entry is one client function that issues an HTTP call. ads-api never talks to Amazon itself: it sends the call to an internal proxy (base URL from an env var, shown as {PROXY_BASE}) whose paths mirror the Amazon Ads API (D52).
proxyResponsibilities: LWA authentication (inferred, the proxy code is not in this repo): the proxy owns the client id/secret and refresh tokens; ads-api sends only internalProxyAuthHeader and never an Amazon Authorization or Amazon-Advertising-API-ClientId header
Region routing: header internalProxyEndpointHeader carries the regional Ads API host chosen from the profile (NA/EU/FE); the proxy calls that host
Scope: Amazon-Advertising-API-Scope = profileId is forwarded as is
Envelope: responses are wrapped as {mess, code, legacyTenantCode, data}; code mirrors the Amazon HTTP status and ads-api checks code (200/207), not the HTTP status of the proxy call
Console session bridge: separate paths (a9g-api-gateway, cm/..., sd/api/v1) forward a logged-in browser session to Amazon Ads console endpoints; those are not Amazon Ads API operations
meta.sellerHubRule: seller-hub calls Amazon directly with each seller own LWA access token. Required headers on v0: Authorization: Bearer <LWA>, Amazon-Advertising-API-ClientId, Amazon-Advertising-API-Scope (profileId). On v1: Authorization, Amazon-Ads-ClientId, Amazon-Ads-AccountId (see catalog/ads/operations.json headers). Region host is chosen per seller account.
caveats: usedBy is found by scanning for calls on AwsService-typed fields; handlers that call the client directly are included (target.go in the handler layer).

amazonOperation is matched on HTTP method + normalised path against catalog/ads/operations.json (generation v0). A match proves the path exists in the spec, not that the request body of ads-api satisfies it.
Budget-rule, optimization-rule and event paths share one client function for sp|sb|sd; the operationId shown is the SP one, SB and SD have sibling operations.
